subject: maths
question: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 18 cm is full of liquid. This liquid is to be filled in cylindrical bottles each of radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. How many bottles are required to empty the bowl?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of bottles (n) = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of one bottle

n = [(2/3) × π × R³] ÷ [π × r² × h]

n = [2 × 18 × 18 × 18] ÷ [3 × 3 × 3 × 6]

n = (2 × 6 × 6) = 72 bottles

**∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Internal radius of hemispherical bowl (R) = 18 cm

Radius of cylindrical bottle (r) = 3 cm

Height of cylindrical bottle (h) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6ec9ff1a6e16c970f168a72863bc310021b329d69fbd7cdc5ba3f6a2edfc7c5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of liquid in bowl = (2/3) × π × (18)³ cm³

⇒ Volume of one bottle = π × (3)² × 6 cm³

⇒ Let n be the number of bottles required.

⇒ n × (Volume of one bottle) = Volume of bowl

⇒ n × (π × 3 × 3 × 6) = (2/3) × π × 18 × 18 × 18

⇒ n = (2 × π × 18 × 18 × 18) ÷ (3 × π × 9 × 6)

⇒ n = (2 × 5832) ÷ (162)

⇒ n = 11664 ÷ 162

⇒ n = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Hemisphere

The TSA of a solid hemisphere includes the curved area and the flat circular base, given by 3πr².

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a complete sphere is double that of a hemisphere, calculated as (4/3)πr³.

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh and Total Surface Area = 2πr(h + r).</p
